beforeRecord.q: Demand is Q=120−3P. Compare P=$30 with P=$10. Which statement explains why a constant slope does not imply constant point elasticity?

afterRecord.feedback: Point elasticity is |dQ/dP| × P/Q. At $30, Q = 30 and |Ed| = 3; at $10, Q = 90 and |Ed| = 1/3. The P/Q ratio changes even though slope is constant. A small price rise lowers revenue at the elastic point and raises it at the inelastic point.
